_note: GAM Research forecast drivers for Gujarat Fluorochemicals (consolidated, Rs crore). Business-line build: fluoropolymers, fluorochemicals, bulk chemicals and other operating revenue share one Chemicals-segment EBITDA margin (the company does not split profit within Chemicals); battery materials (GFCL EV) has its own revenue path and margin. EBITDA is on the Screener annual basis, which excludes net foreign-exchange gains (Rs 88.6 cr in FY26, shown under other income in the annual accounts); we assume no forex gains. Valued on P/E, as most of the street does.

segments.name: Fluoropolymers
segments._why: FY26 +20% (audited; +14.5% on the presentation basis). Q1FY27 +15% YoY to Rs 914 cr. Management guides 15-20% (Q1 call) / 17-20% (closing remarks) a year; plants are nearly full until Rs 250 cr of new capacity and most customer approvals land by end-FY27, with volumes stepping up in H2. 3M's exit has been absorbed; AGC's proposed UK closure is upside not in our numbers. We take the bottom of the range: 15% / 16% / 15%.
segments._marginWhy: Chemicals-segment EBITDA margin (company basis) 24.8% in FY25, 27.3% in FY26 (about 25.5% excluding Rs 88.6 cr of forex gains), 29.1% in Q1FY27 on R32 and a richer fluoropolymer mix. We hold ~29% (29.5% in FY28 with a full year of 20kt R32), ex forex gains.

segments.name: Fluorochemicals (refrigerants, fluorospecialties)
segments._why: Q1FY27 Rs 458 cr (+52% YoY) with the 10kt R32 plant full; annualised that is Rs 1,830 cr (+71%). R32 doubles to 20kt in Q2FY27 and R134a starts by end-FY27, offset by seasonally weaker Q2-Q3 and the R22 phase-down: FY27 +70%. FY28 +18% (full year of 20kt R32, R134a ramp). FY29 +4%: India's HFC freeze from 2028 caps volumes and the 2027 'free year' adds new Indian R32 capacity (Navin +15kt, SRF debottleneck).

segments.name: Bulk chemicals (caustic soda, chloromethanes)
segments._why: Q1FY27 +11% YoY on price; management sees caustic soda stable and chloromethanes range-bound in FY27. Volumes are mostly fixed by plant size.

segments.name: Other operating revenue (export incentives, scrap)
segments._why: Rs 120.6 cr in FY26 (export incentives Rs 78.7 cr). Grows with exports.
segments._marginWhy: Part of the Chemicals segment; the segment margin is measured on revenue including it.

segments.name: Battery materials (GFCL EV)
segments._why: External battery-chemical sales were Rs 15.7 cr in FY26 and Rs 14 cr in Q1FY27. Management targets a three-digit quarterly revenue by Q4FY27 (Q1 call) and 'significant' growth in FY28, with the full potential of the Rs 6,000 cr investment by FY29 at ~2x asset turns. A Jul-2026 plant-visit note quoted Rs 500-700 cr of FY27 revenue at EBITDA break-even, which the Q1 run-rate does not support. We assume Rs 220 cr in FY27, Rs 1,000 cr in FY28 and Rs 2,200 cr in FY29: about a fifth of the stated potential, because qualification has taken longer than planned (Oman project on hold).
segments._marginWhy: Segment EBITDA was -Rs 80 cr in FY26 and -Rs 30 cr in Q1FY27 (fixed costs of ~Rs 40-45 cr a quarter). We assume -50% in FY27 (about -Rs 110 cr), 5% in FY28 and 14% in FY29, against management's 25%+ target at maturity.

_unallocLabel: Forex gains in company EBITDA that the annual accounts show as other income (forecast: none)
_unallocWhy: Company segment EBITDA includes net forex gains (Rs 88.6 cr in FY26); Screener's annual EBITDA, our history, excludes them. We assume no forex gains in forecasts, so no adjustment is needed.
_capexWhy: FY27 earmarked Rs 3,150 cr (annual report): Rs 2,300 cr battery materials (capacity and the new anode plant, relocated from Oman to Dahej) and Rs 850 cr chemicals (Rs 250 cr fluoropolymers, Rs 222 cr electronic chemicals, Rs 150 cr refrigerants, AHF). FY28: the rest of the Rs 6,000 cr cumulative EV plan (~Rs 1,600 cr) plus ~Rs 800 cr chemicals. FY29: Rs 1,500 cr (new HFC capacity cannot be cleared after Dec-2027). FY24-26 actual Rs 1,050-1,125 cr a year.
_depWhy: FY26 depreciation Rs 367 cr; Q1FY27 Rs 102 cr. The model adds all capex to gross block at once (CWIP held flat), so we use 5% to land FY27 depreciation near Rs 450 cr, rising as the battery plants are capitalised.
_treasuryWhy: Net debt, so no treasury income; other income entered separately.
_otherIncomeWhy: Interest, interest subsidy and miscellaneous income ~Rs 40 cr in FY26 excluding Rs 88.6 cr of forex gains; Q1FY27 Rs 12 cr. Includes interest on the unspent IFC money (Rs 340 cr parked at Mar-26).
_interestWhy: FY26 Rs 138 cr; Q1FY27 Rs 26 cr (part capitalised on projects). Net debt rises with Rs 3,150 cr of capex in FY27 and Rs 2,400 cr in FY28; ~7.5% on the average increase, with part capitalised during construction.
_taxWhy: FY26 29%, Q1FY27 29%: battery losses get little tax credit. Falls towards 25-26% as GFCL EV turns profitable.
_payoutWhy: Rs 3 a share for FY26 (5.7% of EPS); cash goes to capex.

dcf._betaWhy: Cyclical chemicals plus an early-stage battery business. The engine discounts at the cost of equity, so we set beta at 0.9 to make the rate (11.9%) equal our WACC: cost of equity 12.5% (beta 1.0), post-tax cost of debt ~5.6%, net debt ~10% of enterprise value at market prices.
dcf._tgWhy: Fluoropolymer and battery-material demand tracks industrial growth and electrification; 6% nominal.
dcf._fadeGrowthWhy: Fluoropolymers ~6-7% a year globally, battery materials faster, refrigerants flat after the HFC freeze.
dcf._fadeCapexWhy: Capex intensity falls from ~50% of revenue in FY27 to ~6% (maintenance plus modest growth) once the battery build-out is done.

bull.label: Bull
bull.narrative: Battery materials ramp closer to management's plan; fluoropolymers grow ~20% a year with AGC's exit; R32 prices hold through the 2027 'free year'.

bear.label: Bear
bear.narrative: Battery qualification slips another year and the business stays loss-making; refrigerant prices fall in the 2027 'free year'; Chinese fluoropolymer competition caps mix gains; Chemicals margin ~26%.

methods.name: P/E
methods.why: How most of the street values GFL: P/E on FY28E earnings (Prabhudas Lilladher 52x; ICICI Direct 30x EV/EBITDA, ~54x P/E). 32x = the stock's one-year-forward P/E median since Apr-2021 excluding trough years (44.5x; FY24-26 left out under the house rule because forward EPS was below half the previous three-year peak; 57.3x including them), cut by the ~28% median de-rating of listed chemical peers against their five-year medians. Growth (~30% a year FY26-28E) matches the low end of what street multiples assume: no further adjustment. Bull 45x = the trough-free median with no sector de-rating; bear 25x = the base cut ~20% for slower growth if the battery ramp slips.

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.why: Counts net debt explicitly, which matters as borrowings rise with Rs 5,500 cr of capex in FY27-28. 20x = GFL's five-year trailing EV/EBITDA median (28.6x) less the same ~29% sector de-rating seen in peers' EV/EBITDA. Not cleaned of trough years, so it sits above the P/E target.

methods.name: DCF
methods.why: Tests whether cash flows support the price: 15-year FCFF at 11.9%, terminal growth 6%, working capital held at the FY26 ratio of revenue.
